title: LEGO designer rebuilds viral raccoon 'Jimothy' from Grey Wolf set
summary: A LEGO Senior Design Manager has recreated internet-famous short-spined raccoon Jimothy using only parts from the official 31393 Grey Wolf set.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Jordan Scott, a Senior Design Manager, has built a custom model of Jimothy, the short-spined raccoon that's gone viral online, using only pieces from the official 31393 Grey Wolf set (657 pieces, £44.99 / $49.99 / €49.99, out now).

According to Brick Fanatics, the build reworks the raccoon element already included in Grey Wolf, shortening its body to match Jimothy's distinctive look. No official instructions have been released, but it's confirmed that no extra or modified parts were used beyond what comes in the standard set.

Jimothy himself isn't LEGO-related at all — he's a real raccoon spotted in Seattle with what experts believe is a spinal deformity, though he's said to be healthy. His unusual appearance has made him a viral hit across gaming and pop culture this week, and now the brick-building world too.

## Why it matters
It's a fun reminder of how flexible official LEGO sets can be for custom building — fans (and even LEGO's own designers) can repurpose animal-themed sets like Grey Wolf for creative alternate builds. For UK builders and collectors, it's also a nudge that 31393 Grey Wolf offers good part variety for animal MOCs beyond its intended design.

## What to watch next
There's no confirmed plan for an official LEGO Jimothy set or promotion, so any further builds, instructions, or social media follow-ups remain speculative for now.

For UK collectors and display builders, this is a notable shift for a growing modular-style theme. Widening the street beyond Spider-Man opens the door to more varied Marvel buildings, which could make the collection more appealing to a broader range of fans and easier to display alongside other modular-style builds.

title: Deadline looms for LEGO Ideas' 'Hidden Secrets' GWP contest

bodyMarkdown:

Entries must avoid using any licensed IPs, including LEGO's own themes, must be no more than 250 pieces, and can include a maximum of two minifigures. It's worth building in some buffer time before the deadline too, as entries that break the rules may need resubmitting.

The grand prize includes the model becoming an official LEGO set, ten copies of the finished product, a design credit and bio as LEGO Ideas Fan Designer, plus a mystery prize. Everyone who reaches the voting stage will also receive 10351 Sherlock Holmes Book Nook and 21362 Minerals Collection as a reward.

## Why it matters
LEGO Ideas is one of the few routes for fan designers to see their own creations turned into official retail sets, and GWP contests like this one carry extra appeal since gift-with-purchase sets are often smaller, characterful builds that get plenty of attention when they land. For UK fans who enjoy designing or entering community contests, this is a low-cost way to potentially get a model produced.

## What happened
The LEGO Group has officially revealed minifigures for a wave of new Marvel sets tied to Avengers: Doomsday. The lineup includes 76347 Avengers: Doomsday Quinjet (four minifigures, among them MCU-style Cyclops and a shirtless The Thing), 76348 Epic Battle: Avengers: Doomsday (six minifigures including several new X-Men characters), and 76352 Avengers Doomsday: New Avengers Tower (six minifigures covering New Avengers characters). Notably, Doctor Doom returns to LEGO Marvel for the first time since 76005 Spider-Man: Daily Bugle Showdown retired back in 2014 — he'll appear in both movie and comic-accurate minifigure forms, including in the 76340 LEGO Marvel Advent Calendar 2026. Mr Fantastic also gets a rework, swapping the stilt-like long-leg assembly from 76316 Fantastic Four vs. Galactus for proper minifigure legs and a more accurate face print. Printed legs feature across most of the new figures, which remains relatively uncommon for LEGO Marvel sets.

## Why it matters
This is a strong showing for LEGO Marvel collectors, with Doctor Doom's long-awaited return likely to be a highlight for anyone who's followed the theme for years. ## What happened
Designer Carl Merriam, who worked on 72051 Donkey Kong Arcade alongside sets like 71411 The Mighty Bowser and 10497 Galaxy Explorer, has spoken to The Verge about building LEGO's recreation of the classic 1981 arcade cabinet.

Merriam revealed that controlling the barrels' speed was the toughest challenge, saying he 'rolled thousands of barrels down those tracks' during development. The team also tried various ways of returning barrels to the top, including gears and levers, before settling on a simpler solution — just using more barrels. The finished chute holds 14 barrels with room for up to 20, creating what Merriam calls an 'infinite barrel loop'.
